name: Tannheimer Tal
kurzbeschreibung: The Tannheimer Tal at 1,100 m in the Allgäu Alps is hailed as Europe's most enchanting high valley, featuring Lake Vilsalpsee, Haldensee, cable cars, and limestone peaks.
beschreibung:
Überblick

The breathtaking Tannheimer Tal rests at an elevation of 1,100 metres within the Allgäu Alps of the Tyrolean Außerfern district, widely celebrated by alpine authors as Europe's most picturesque high valley. Extending roughly 16 kilometres from Nesselwängle in the east through Grän, Tannheim, and Zöblen to Schattwald on the Bavarian border, this wide glacial trough pairs rolling pastoral pastures with formidable limestone battlements. It is flanked by the jagged peaks of Rote Flüh (2,108 m), Gimpel, and Kellenspitze on the north side, counterbalanced by gentle grassy summits like Mount Neunerköpfle to the south. Glittering alpine tarns including the protected emerald Vilsalpsee and the swimming waters of Lake Haldensee enhance the scenery. Cableways in Tannheim, Grän, and Schattwald provide swift access to high ridges. In summer, over 300 kilometres of trails feature highlights such as the 'largest summit logbook in the Alps'. In winter, it transforms into an internationally lauded cross-country skiing hub.

Route & Anforderungen

The valley provides walking options for every ambition. Casual strollers enjoy the level valley floor path shadowing the Vils stream connecting villages (1 to 3 hours, level paved or packed gravel tracks). Mountaineers can undertake the classic ascent to the Gimpelhaus and the summit of Rote Flüh (approx. 3.5 hours, 850 m ascent, alpine sure-footedness required). Standard sneakers suffice for the floor; supportive lugged mountain boots are mandatory for ridgelines. The valley floor tracks and Haldensee promenade are completely stroller-friendly.

Besuch & Anreise

Motorists arrive via the Fern Pass route (B179) and B199 over the Gaicht Pass from Reutte, or toll-free from Bavaria via the A7 motorway and Oberjoch pass. Ample pay parking exists at all lift terminals. Rail travelers alight at Sonthofen (Bavaria) or Reutte in Tirol, connecting via regular regional buses straight into the valley.

Tipps

Ascend the Neunerköpfle gondola to sign the 'World's Largest Summit Book' perched near the top station, then walk the sensory 9erlebnisweg trail before stopping at the rustic Gundhütte for cheese spätzle.
preis: Valley walking routes and lakes free; cable cars approx. €24-28 round trip (complimentary with partner hotels in summer)
oeffnungszeiten: Valley trails open year-round; summer lift operations run May to October; winter ski season December to April
saison: Ganzjährig zugänglich (Sommersaison Mai bis Oktober ideal)
